Both sides took to the pitch determined to claim all three points in a high-stakes football encounter. A Tense First Half Early exchanges saw both teams engaging in a physical battle, with tactical discipline taking precedence over creative flair. While Telstar earned numerous corner kicks, Jeff Hardeveld was unable to connect with his teammates in the box. The Heracles defense held firm, and despite a few attempts to break the deadlock, the sides entered the interval with the scoreline untouched, reflecting a cagey and methodical approach from both managers. Breaking the Deadlock The second half proved to be a completely different spectacle, as the game opened up and quality in the final third began to shine through. Guus Offerhaus provided the spark in the 70th minute, burying a right-footed shot to give the hosts the lead. The floodgates opened quickly thereafter: Tyrese Noslin doubled the advantage just two minutes later following a clever assist from Patrick Brouwer . Before the visitors could recover, Jeff Hardeveld rose to head home a third goal in the 77th minute, delighting the 5,142 fans in attendance. Late Drama The closing stages were marred by frustration for the visitors. As Heracles searched for a consolation goal, the match turned sour in stoppage time. Following a VAR review, Luka Kulenovic was shown a straight red card in the 92nd minute for a reckless challenge on Nils Rossen , effectively ending any hopes of a late comeback and cementing the 3-0 scoreline.

The Primeira Liga action continued on 2026-05-12 as Tondela welcomed irense for a highly anticipated encounter. Both teams took to the pitch with clear tactical objectives, looking to assert dominance in a match that would eventually be defined by clinical finishing and late drama. Aiko Gives Tondela the Edge The match began with irense attempting to dictate play, but it was Tondela who showed superior clinical edge. In the 18th minute, the deadlock was broken when Pedro Henryque provided a pinpoint assist for Makan Aiko , who slotted the ball home with his right foot. The goal energized the home crowd, and Tondela nearly doubled their lead just before the interval. In the 44th minute, Rony Lopes unleashed a delicate lob that beat the goalkeeper but rattled off the crossbar, much to the relief of the visitors. irense did have their chances to equalize, most notably a header from Kiko Bondoso that required a steady save from Bernardo Fontes . However, despite enjoying the lion's share of possession, the visitors struggled to break down a resilient Tondela defense, heading into the break trailing by a single goal. Lopes Seals the Result Amidst Late Chaos The second half saw Tondela maintain their discipline while waiting for the perfect moment to strike again. That moment arrived in the 60th minute when Tiago Manso set up Rony Lopes , who found the back of the net with a powerful left-footed strike to make it 2-0. irense responded with a wave of tactical substitutions, bringing on Luis Semedo and Cedric Teguia , but the hosts remained compact and organized. As the clock ticked towards full-time, the atmosphere grew increasingly heated. The stoppage time period was marred by several incidents, leading to yellow cards for Cedric Teguia and Jordan Pefok . The tension reached its boiling point in the 94th minute when the referee showed a direct red card to Maracas for unsportsmanlike conduct. Despite irense finishing with 60% possession, Tondela walked away with a deserved 2-0 victory, showcasing a masterclass in efficiency.

Following the interval, Juventus pushed to extend their lead, and they succeeded in the 54th minute when Dusan Vlahovic netted his second of the game, finishing a well-constructed move assisted by Chico Conceição . The Fightback and Final Drama Trailing by two, the hosts refused to concede defeat and ramped up their tactical aggression. Cesare Casadei sparked hope in the 60th minute, leaping to head home a dangerous delivery from Rafael Obrador . The game turned into a frantic battle as both managers introduced fresh legs to influence the outcome. The pressure finally told in the 84th minute, as Che Adams reacted quickest to a loose ball, slotting home to level the score. Despite a series of late tactical changes and mounting tension in stoppage time, both sides had to settle for a share of the spoils in a hard-fought Serie A clash.

matches.description: Watch Torino vs Sassuolo highlights and goals from Serie A on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 8, 2026. On 2026-05-08, the Stadio Olimpico Grande Torino played host to a captivating Serie A clash between Torino and Sassuolo . Both teams entered the pitch with clear tactical objectives, setting the stage for a contest defined by discipline and sudden shifts in momentum. Defensive Resilience in the Opening Period The first half was a testament to organized defending, with both sides struggling to break the deadlock despite several set-piece opportunities. Sassuolo came closest to an opener in the 14th minute when Tarik Muharemovic saw his goal-bound effort hacked off the line by the Torino defense following an Armand Lauriente corner. While the hosts controlled periods of possession, their delivery from wide areas often failed to find a teammate, leaving the 18,000 fans in attendance waiting for the first breakthrough at the interval. A Dramatic Turnaround in the Second Half The game exploded into life shortly after the restart. In the 51st minute, Sassuolo took the lead as Kristian Thorstvedt found space to tap home a Luca Lipani assist with his left foot. This goal prompted Torino into a double substitution, bringing on Duvan Zapata and Marcus Holmgren Pedersen to sharpen their attack. The tactical shift paid dividends in the 66th minute when Giovanni Simeone rose highest to head home an equalizer following a cross from Enzo Ebosse . The momentum had firmly shifted, and just four minutes later, Torino struck again. Nikola Vlasic played a short corner to set up Marcus Holmgren Pedersen , who powered a header into the back of the net to make it 2-1. Despite late pressure from the visitors—including a missed header from Ulisses Garcia in stoppage time—and a flurry of yellow cards for Niels Nkounkou and Gvidas Gineitis , the home side held firm to secure a hard-fought victory.
